quote: I cannot say there is no vanity in making this funeral oration of myself, but I hope it is not a misplaced one; and this is a matter of fact which is easily cleared and ascertained.
source: David Hume, My Own Life, the closing sentence, dated April 18, 1776, in The Life of David Hume, Esq. (Strahan, 1777)

evidence.where: Wikisource transcription, proofread against the page scans, of The Life of David Hume, Esq. Written by Himself (London: W. Strahan and T. Cadell, 1777), section My Own Life; the rendered text was fetched and the closing sentence matched word for word, followed by the dateline April 18, 1776
evidence.edition: The Life of David Hume, Esq. Written by Himself, London, W. Strahan and T. Cadell, 1777
evidence.locator: My Own Life, the last sentence, immediately before the dateline April 18, 1776

reason: The wording is the 1777 first printing's, the closing sentence of the autobiography Hume wrote four months before his death. Hume has no lines in the year and is clear of the cap; a cheerful self-written funeral oration fits a month on mortality.
